gaps.hint: person needed (-ist for fields of study)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ist forms the person who studies a subject: biology becomes biologist.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (SURVIVE) of the species is under threat.
gaps.explanation: The noun from SURVIVE is 'survival'; a survivor is a person.

gaps.sentence: The medicine is available without a ___ (PRESCRIBE).
The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: Club ___ (MEMBER) costs fifty euros a year.
gaps.explanation: "Membership costs" — the fee noun, not the person.
The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unusual. An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: We had a ___ view of the coast from the plane (SPECTACLE).
gaps.explanation: The adjective of 'spectacle' is spectacular; it modifies the noun 'view'.

gaps.sentence: The train arrived ___ , despite the snow (PUNCTUAL).
gaps.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'arrived': punctually (-ly). 'Punctuality' is the noun.
